title: News Aggregator
seoTitle: Design a News Aggregator Like Google News
description: Design a news aggregator — crawling publisher feeds, deduplicating stories, and serving a fast paginated feed of recent articles by category.
author: Editorial Team

blocks.title: What is a News Aggregator?
blocks.text: A news aggregator (like Google News) collects articles from thousands of publishers, groups them, and shows users a single feed of the latest stories — linking out to the original publisher to read the full article.

items: Users should be able to view a feed of recent articles, newest first.
Users should be able to filter the feed by category (e.g. Technology, Sports).
Users should be able to page through the feed with infinite scroll.
Clicking an article should take the user to the publisher's site.
User accounts, comments and saved articles.

blocks.question: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?

items: New articles should appear within ~30 minutes of publication.
The feed should load fast (< 200ms) and be highly available.
The system should scale to 100M daily users with traffic spikes during breaking news.
The same story shouldn't appear multiple times from syndicated copies.

blocks.text: There are two halves: an **ingestion pipeline** that pulls content in, and a **serving path** that's overwhelmingly read-heavy. We'll design each, then go deep on freshness, pagination and caching.

items: **Publisher**: a news source with one or more RSS/Atom feeds.
**Article**: title, summary, thumbnail URL, link, category, publishedAt.

blocks.text: Clicks go straight to the publisher URL; if we want click tracking, we can redirect through `GET /articles/:id/visit -> 302`.

A **Feed Collector** fetches each publisher's RSS feed on a schedule, parses new entries, and writes Articles to the database. Thumbnails are downloaded once and stored in blob storage so we don't hotlink publisher images.
2) Users should be able to view and filter the feed
A **Feed Service** queries the latest articles, optionally filtered by category, ordered by `publishedAt DESC`, and returns a page plus a cursor.
1) How do we keep the feed fresh without hammering publishers?

approach.text: Fetch every one of ~50k publisher feeds on a fixed short interval.

challenges.text: Most feeds haven't changed, so the vast majority of requests are wasted, and aggressive polling can get us rate-limited or blocked by publishers.

approach.text: Poll each feed at an interval based on how often it publishes (busy outlets every few minutes, quiet blogs hourly), and use `ETag` / `If-Modified-Since` headers so unchanged feeds return a cheap `304 Not Modified`.

challenges.text: Still polling, so freshness is bounded by each feed's interval — but well within our 30-minute target.

blocks.title: Adaptive polling plus push where available

approach.text: Subscribe via **WebSub** (PubSubHubbub) for publishers that support it so new articles are pushed to us instantly; fall back to adaptive polling for everyone else. Collectors are sharded by publisher and fed from a scheduling queue.

challenges.text: Push endpoints need verification and must be idempotent, since the same item can arrive by both push and poll.

blocks.text: 2) How do we paginate a feed that keeps changing?

challenges.text: New articles arriving at the top shift everything down, so users see duplicates when they scroll. Large offsets are also slow.

approach.text: Return a cursor encoding the last article's `(publishedAt, id)` and query `WHERE (published_at, id) < (:ts, :id) ORDER BY published_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20`. With an index on `(category, published_at, id)` each page is a fast index range scan, and new articles never cause duplicates.

challenges.text: You can't jump to an arbitrary page number — which infinite scroll doesn't need.

blocks.text: 3) How do we serve 100M users and survive breaking-news spikes?

Everyone sees the same feed for a given category, which makes it extremely cacheable. Precompute the first few pages of each category feed into Redis whenever new articles are ingested, and put a **CDN** in front of the feed API with a short TTL (30-60 seconds). During a spike, nearly all requests are served from the edge and the database barely notices.

Deduplicate syndicated stories (the same wire story on 40 sites) during ingestion: normalise the title and compute a similarity hash (e.g. SimHash) over the text, and group near-duplicates so the feed shows one entry.

quiz.question: Why is offset pagination a problem for a live news feed?
options: It is not supported by SQL
New articles shift results and cause duplicates while scrolling
quiz.explanation: Cursor pagination anchors on the last item seen, so inserts at the top don't affect later pages.

quiz.question: What do ETag / If-Modified-Since headers save when polling RSS feeds?
options: Unchanged feeds return a cheap 304 instead of the full body
They remove the need for a scheduler
quiz.explanation: Conditional requests make polling an unchanged feed nearly free for both sides.

quiz.question: Why does a non-personalised feed scale so well?
options: Every user sees the same pages, so they can be cached at a CDN
quiz.explanation: Shared responses can be served from edge caches with short TTLs.

quiz.question: How can syndicated copies of the same story be grouped?
options: Similarity hashing such as SimHash over normalised text
quiz.explanation: Near-duplicate detection catches the same wire story published on many sites with small edits.
